tour.title: Main App Shell
tour.description: The root page.js is the heart of StayFit — a monolithic 2762-line component that owns all application state: food logging, calorie/macro tracking, the AI scan modal, custom food entry, and the food library. Every user interaction flows through this file, which acts as the controller that wires together all UI widgets and API calls. Understanding this file gives you the complete picture of what the app does before zooming into individual pieces.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router uses file-based routing — a file at app/page.js automatically becomes the '/' route. Naming a component file page.js makes it a route segment, while layout.js wraps all routes beneath it.

tour.title: Project Dependencies
tour.description: The package.json declares the full technology stack: Next.js 15 for the framework, React for UI, @google/generative-ai for Gemini AI integration, googleapis for Sheets access, chart.js and react-chartjs-2 for data visualization, and @dnd-kit for drag-and-drop food reordering. Reading the dependencies before diving into code reveals what problems each library solves and why those choices were made.
tour.languageLesson: NPM package.json separates dependencies (needed at runtime) from devDependencies (only needed during development). Next.js, React, and googleapis belong in dependencies; ESLint and type checkers belong in devDependencies.

tour.title: App Layout & PWA Shell
tour.description: The layout.js wraps every page in the app, setting up global metadata, font loading (via next/font), and Vercel Analytics. Alongside it, manifest.js defines the PWA web app manifest that makes StayFit installable on mobile home screens — specifying the app name, theme color, icons, and standalone display mode. These two files together create the 'app shell' that users perceive before any page-level code runs.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router special files: layout.js defines persistent UI wrapping all child routes; manifest.js exports a function returning a WebAppManifest object that Next.js serves as /manifest.webmanifest automatically.

tour.title: Global Styles & Tailwind
tour.description: The globals.css establishes the visual foundation using Tailwind CSS directives and CSS custom properties for the color palette, spacing, and typography. The tailwind.config.js extends the default Tailwind theme with the app's custom colors and font families, while postcss.config.js wires Tailwind into the PostCSS build pipeline. All component styling in the app builds on top of these definitions.
tour.languageLesson: Tailwind's @layer directive (base, components, utilities) controls CSS specificity and purge behavior. Custom properties (CSS variables) in :root allow runtime theming while still using Tailwind utility classes that reference those variables.

tour.title: Vietnamese Food Database
tour.description: The common-foods.js file is the offline data backbone of StayFit — a static array of 200+ Vietnamese dishes and ingredients, each with name, unit, serving size, calories, protein, carbs, and fat. The root page.js imports this directly, using it as the food picker library and as a reference corpus for fuzzy-matching AI-identified food names against known nutritional values. This file is what makes the app work offline without any API call.

tour.title: Google Sheets Data Layer
tour.description: The sync route is the primary data persistence layer for the entire application. Its GET handler reads the user's profile, weight history, and food log from a Google Sheet; its POST handler writes updates back; and its DELETE handler removes log entries. Because Google Sheets is the sole database (no SQL, no ORM), every piece of user data flows through this single route. The app/page.js calls this route on load and after every user action.
tour.languageLesson: Using Google Sheets as a database is a common 'spreadsheet as backend' pattern for personal tools. The googleapis Node.js client authenticates via a service account JSON key. safeFloat() in this file handles Vietnamese locale decimals written with commas (e.g. '81,4') — raw parseFloat would return NaN.

tour.title: Meal Persistence API
tour.description: The save-meal route handles the specific action of appending a new food log entry as a row in the Google Sheets spreadsheet. It is a focused POST-only handler, separate from the broader sync route, because meal logging is the most frequent write operation and benefits from being a lightweight, single-purpose endpoint. The root page.js calls this whenever the user confirms a food selection.

tour.title: AI Food Recognition
tour.description: StayFit offers two AI-powered food identification routes built on Google Gemini. The text-analyze route accepts a food name description and uses Gemini text generation to identify the food and look up its nutrition, while the vision-analyze route accepts a base64-encoded photo and uses Gemini's vision capabilities to identify what's in the image. Both routes apply fuzzy Vietnamese name matching — diacritic-stripping normalization plus token-Jaccard similarity scoring — to map Gemini's output back to entries in the local food database.
tour.languageLesson: Fuzzy string matching for Vietnamese text requires diacritic normalization because 'pho' and 'phở' are the same dish but differ in Unicode codepoints. The Jaccard similarity on token sets (intersection/union) tolerates word reordering and partial matches better than Levenshtein distance for food names.

tour.title: API Rate Limiting
tour.description: The middleware.js runs before every API route request and enforces in-memory rate limits: 30 requests per minute for general routes and 10 per minute for AI endpoints (text-analyze and vision-analyze). This protects against runaway Gemini API costs and accidental abuse. Being in-memory means limits reset on server restart — by design for a personal app, but worth knowing if the app ever scales to multiple instances.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js middleware runs at the Edge before the route handler, making it ideal for cross-cutting concerns like auth and rate limiting. The middleware.js file at the project root is automatically applied to all matching routes via the exported config.matcher array.

tour.title: Security & Build Config
tour.description: The next.config.js adds security HTTP response headers across all routes: a Content Security Policy (CSP) restricts which external scripts can run, X-Frame-Options prevents clickjacking, HSTS enforces HTTPS, and Permissions-Policy blocks browser APIs the app does not use. These headers are applied via Next.js's headers() config function and require no runtime code. This file is worth reading to understand the security posture of the deployed app.

tour.title: Dashboard Layout
tour.description: The dashboard/page.js is a secondary route that assembles a read-only analytics view of the user's fitness data. It imports and composes six widgets — CalorieCircle, MacroDonut, FoodLogSection, WeeklyTrendCard, GreetingHeader, and BreathingTimer — into a single dashboard layout. Unlike the root page.js, the dashboard page does not manage state itself; it receives data as props or via shared state and delegates all rendering to the individual components.

tour.title: Calorie & Macro Visualization
tour.description: CalorieCircle renders an SVG progress ring that fills as the user's logged calories approach their daily goal — the primary at-a-glance metric. MacroDonut renders a Chart.js doughnut chart showing the protein/carb/fat breakdown of the day's food log. These two components appear together at the top of both the root page and the dashboard, forming the key 'how am I doing today' visual summary that the whole app is built around.
tour.languageLesson: SVG stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset are the standard technique for animating circular progress rings: set dasharray to the circumference and animate dashoffset from full (empty) to zero (full). Chart.js is initialized in a useEffect with a cleanup to destroy the canvas instance and avoid memory leaks on re-renders.

tour.title: Food Log Components
tour.description: FoodLogSection groups the day's food entries by meal type (breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack) and renders a list of FoodLogItem components. Each FoodLogItem shows a single logged food entry with its nutritional values and provides edit and delete action buttons that call back up to the parent state in app/page.js. This two-level component hierarchy — section containing items — keeps the list manageable and makes it easy to add per-meal subtotals.

tour.title: Weekly Trend & Shared Card
tour.description: WeeklyTrendCard displays a Chart.js bar chart of the past 7 days of calorie intake, letting users spot patterns in their eating habits over time. It wraps its content in DashboardCard, the generic card wrapper used by every dashboard widget to provide consistent padding, rounded corners, and shadow styling. DashboardCard's high fan-in (imported by three different consumers) shows it is the visual design primitive that unifies the whole dashboard.

tour.title: Wellness Features & Greeting
tour.description: GreetingHeader renders a personalized time-based welcome message (good morning / good afternoon / good evening) using the user's name from their profile. BreathingTimer is an animated guided breathing exercise — cycling through inhale, hold, and exhale phases — adding a wellness dimension beyond pure calorie counting. Together these components reflect StayFit's philosophy that fitness tracking should feel personal and holistic, not just a number-crunching tool.
